changes.description: Raised PDF extraction, upload, bookmark/link, download, Android upload, and text-layout admission limits to 3000 pages / 300 MiB; added explicit Korean and English PDF-limit errors.

Files above 1 MiB extract through one queued Node worker with a 384 MiB old-generation heap limit, transferable input copy, per-page decode deadlines and HTTP-thread watchdog; all extraction yields between pages, cleans each page, and clears document caches every 30 pages. Worker progress callbacks report completed physical pages. Large uploads reuse the extraction first-page title/DOI/arXiv metadata rather than parsing a book twice on the HTTP thread.

Books over 300 pages use persisted inclusive translation ranges of at most 30 pages, preserving earlier sections across continuation. Legacy whole-book starts default to pages 1–30; restart/resume cannot bypass section limits. Desktop offers a From/Through dialog, current page–current+29 defaults, next-30 continuation, source-page fallback, and Translate this section.

Book snapshots default to 30 pages and accept pageStart/pageEnd; SQLite filters block regions before JSON decoding. Android caches one bounded window and refreshes as the active reading pane moves. Ordinary <=300-page snapshots retain the legacy shape. Large PDF range responses stream files and cache hash verification by file stat identity, preserving changed-cache refusal.

Desktop canvases were already virtualized; removed eager all-page dimension fetching for books and clean page resources on unmount. Scripted browser opens and jumps to page 1232 keep two canvases mounted. Android LazyColumn and file-backed PDF download/cache require no rendering changes.

Book structure detection reuses ingested page-local figure/table/equation geometry in background batches separated by 5 ms yields. This avoids a second image-heavy PDF decode and retaining every text run; normal paper detectors remain intact. Generated fixtures and reproducible measurement scripts are committed, while generated PDFs stay in temporary directories.

measurements.notes: RSS is the hub/benchmark Node process high-water mark, including upload buffers and worker threads, excluding separate Chrome processes and fixture-generation subprocess allocations. Upload/extract time includes HTTP transfer and storage. Each image page embeds a unique 128x128 RGB image and 30 text lines. Temp fixtures are removed after the run.

coverage: Generated 400-page extraction, generated 3001-page rejection, per-page progress, HTTP pings below 200 ms during extraction, worker timeout/recovery with caller input preserved, 1232-page snapshot windows, range-only translation and continuation without deleting earlier translations, streaming large-PDF ranges and hash-cache invalidation.
limitations: No physical Android device or instrumented emulator run; Android unit tests/build pass and existing LazyColumn/file streaming were inspected. No emulator was modified.
The 300 MiB maximum-sized fixture was not benchmarked; measured image fixture is 64,579,633 bytes. RSS is bounded by one extraction worker plus inputs/results, not a fixed whole-process RSS ceiling.
For books, supplemental citation-marker extraction that needs another all-page text pass is skipped; ingested figure/equation geometry remains available through incremental structure detection.
Android keeps the most recently fetched 30-page metadata/translation window for offline use; the original PDF and annotations remain locally available independently.

Real subscription-provider answers were not requested; existing question text limits and full-book retrieval behavior are unchanged, while normal fake-provider question flows pass e2e. Image-question transport and selection geometry were not edited.
Scanned-only books retain existing no-OCR behavior; source PDF reading remains available. Long-book translated-PDF export was not exercised.
